title: Telegram photos: send as media (inline photo) with JPEG compression + 24h cached upload log
author: the operator
trigger: Operator at farm on 2026-09-13 confirmed: (1) Telegram alerts arrive but the photos render as a downloadable file rather than inline media. The cause is telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py:99 which sets type='document' (file) instead of type='photo' (media). (2) Vehicle alerts timed out (httpx.WriteTimeout) because TG#1 uploads ~13 MB of full-resolution PNG (composite.png + frame_004.png) and the 10s httpx timeout is too tight for residential upload. (3) Operator wants the bytes actually sent to Telegram to be recoverable for troubleshooting — i.e., a cached copy on disk alongside the alert artifact directory, retained 24h.
background: The zero-JPEG rule from US-019 only applies to canonical on-disk artifacts (the source PNGs in data/frames/<alert_id>/). The Telegram upload path is a delivery channel, not a canonical store: compressing the upload to JPEG q=88 with 1920px max-dim cuts wire size ~15x while leaving the lossless PNG untouched on disk. Inline photo rendering via type='photo' requires JPEG (Telegram re-encodes uploaded PNG to JPEG anyway when type='photo' is used). Switching to type='photo' resolves the rendering problem AND the timeout problem simultaneously, with the on-disk PNG still preserved per the zero-JPEG rule.
shipping_definition: All US-030 stories marked done; pytest 49/49 (or higher) green; tree clean; telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py:99 changed from type='document' to type='photo'; pre-upload JPEG conversion added (q=88, max-dim 1920px); cached JPEGs written to data/tg_uploads/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<alert_id>/ with 24h retention sweep on boot and every hour via existing watchdog tick; structured single-line tg-send log on success AND failure including source paths+bytes, converted paths+bytes+quality+maxdim, cache paths, upload bytes, elapsed seconds, response status; daemon.log shows the new log line format on the next alert; operator can ls data/tg_uploads/<date>/<alert_id>/ and see the exact JPEG that was sent.
scope_exclusions: Changing the canonical on-disk PNG format is NOT this PRD — zero-JPEG rule for canonical artifacts (US-019) is unchanged. JPEG applies only to the Telegram upload channel.
Adding a local HTTP server for sendPhoto with photo=http_url is NOT this PRD — direct multipart upload stays.
Adding Telegram thumbnail/preview generation is NOT this PRD.
Changing the existing alert_id UUID structure is NOT this PRD.
Adding a generic image cache unrelated to Telegram delivery is NOT this PRD — the cache is strictly tg_uploads/<date>/<alert_id>/.
Changing httpx timeouts is NOT this PRD — the JPEG compression eliminates the timeout trigger for the standard alert size.

US-030a.title: Telegram photo delivery: convert to inline media (type=photo) with JPEG q=88 + 1920px max-dim, cache 24h, structured log

verification_checklist: telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py:99 changed from type='document' to type='photo'
Pre-upload conversion: cv2 or PIL reads source PNG, writes JPEG q=88 max-dim 1920px to data/tg_uploads/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<alert_id>/<n>.jpg
Conversion errors raise cleanly (no silent fall-through to PNG upload)
Cached JPEGs are written BEFORE the network upload so troubleshooting data exists even if upload fails
24h retention sweep: on boot AND every hour via existing watchdog tick, delete data/tg_uploads/<date>/ where date < (today - 1 day)

Structured single-line log on success: 'tg-send: alert_id=... TG#N chat=... method=sendMediaGroup type=photo sources=[(path,size),...] converted=[(jpg_path,size,q,maxdim),...] cache=[(path,size),...] upload=<total_bytes> elapsed=<s> response=HTTP <code>'
Structured single-line log on failure: same fields + error=<exception class>: <message>
tests/test_dispatcher.py extended: (1) test type=photo in payload, (2) test JPEG conversion with mocked PNG input, (3) test cache directory creation, (4) test log line format on success + failure

Live verification: trigger any alert on any camera; confirm daemon.log shows the new tg-send line format; confirm data/tg_uploads/<date>/<alert_id>/ exists with the converted JPEGs; confirm the Telegram message renders the photo inline (not as a file)
Sweep verification: artificially age a cache directory's mtime to >24h ago; trigger sweep via /debug/refresh or restart; confirm the directory is removed
manual_override_notes: If a particular alert's source PNG is smaller than the JPEG equivalent (rare; only happens for already-compressed or tiny images), the conversion still runs (writes a JPEG that's slightly larger). This is acceptable — the cost is small and consistency wins.
references: logs/daemon.log (2026-09-12 09:33-09:34 — actual WriteTimeout evidence from operator visit)
